{"stage":{"done_when":"A finished poem of at least 10 lines in which at least three lines break in the middle of a sentence.","learn":"how line breaks shape meaning","practice":"write a poem that uses enjambment","skill":"Poetry"},"work":{"kind":"poem","text":"The ferry leaves before the light
has made up its mind about the water,
and the gulls, who have opinions
about everything, follow it out
past the cranes, past the long wall
where my father fished for nothing
every Sunday of my childhood,
and come back with the morning
folded under their wings, as if
they had paid for it.","title":"Harbour"}}

{"stage":{"done_when":"A finished poem of at least 10 lines in which at least three lines break in the middle of a sentence.","learn":"how line breaks shape meaning","practice":"write a poem that uses enjambment","skill":"Poetry"},"work":{"kind":"poem","text":"My father fished on Sunday mornings.
He never caught a single fish.
The sea was grey and so was he.
He sat there with his flask of tea.
The gulls came down to watch him wait.
He always said the fish were late.
We walked home slowly, hand in hand.
I didn't really understand.
I do now, standing where he stood.
The waiting was the thing he loved.","title":"Sunday"}}

Ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, sliced; 1 red pepper, sliced; 1 onion, sliced; 2 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp oil; 1 tsp grated ginger.

1. Heat the oil in a wok over high heat for 1 minute.
2. Fry the chicken for 5 minutes until cooked through.
3. Add the pepper, onion and ginger and fry for 3 minutes.
4. Add the soy sauce and cook for 30 seconds more, then serve.","title":"Chicken stir-fry"}}
